Perfect! This is a clean win. **Nb6+** is a check that forces Black into a losing position:
- If Rxb6, White recaptures with Bxb6 or axb6, winning a rook
- If Black plays any king move, White simply plays Nxa8, winning the rook cleanly

This is a classic **fork** motif—the knight on b6 gives check to the king and simultaneously attacks the undefended rook on a8.

**Best move:** Nb6+

**Main line:** Nb6+ Rxb6 (or any king move allows Nxa8) Bxb6 and White has won a full rook

**Motif:** fork

**Explanation (coaching note):**

When your opponent moves the rook to b3, check if their undefended pieces are vulnerable. Here, the rook on a8 and king are on the same diagonal-like pattern. A knight jump to b6 gives check AND attacks the rook simultaneously—a textbook fork. Black must lose material either way: if they capture the knight, you recapture and keep the extra exchange; if they move the king, you simply take the free rook. Look for moves that attack the king AND hit something else at the same time.
